words.trans: adj. 铸铁的，生铁铸造的
examples: An old cast-iron pan.
a cast-iron bridge.

words.trans: n. 懒骨头，懒家伙（口语，单复数同形）
examples: Go and get the map, lazybones.
Come on, lazybones!

words.trans: n. 英国地形测量局；Ordnance Survey map 英国官方详细地形图，简写 OS map
examples: Joel fetched an Ordnance Survey map.
a detailed Ordnance Survey map of the area.

words.trans: v. 逐渐变细，向远方收窄
examples: The ribbon of the Elleray tapered away to the west.
The road tapers to a track.

words.trans: n. 一大片土地或区域（a swathe of forest 一大片森林）
examples: A swathe of brown showed the high fells.
a wide swathe of forest.

words.trans: n. 林地，树林区域
examples: Patches of green indicated woodland.
a woodland walk.

words.trans: adj. 无休止的，持续不断的；毫不松懈的，不会减弱的
examples: The relentless march of the contour lines.
The rain fell relentlessly.

words.trans: n. 轮廓；（地图）等高线（contour lines 地图等高线）
examples: The relentless march of the contour lines.
a contour map.

words.trans: n. 槽；U形山谷洼地
examples: It stopped in a deep U-shaped trough.
The boat pitched into a trough.

words.trans: adj. 锯齿状的，凹凸嶙峋的
examples: A trough framed by jagged ridges.
jagged rocks.

words.trans: n. 山脊
examples: Up that ridge.
We climbed to the ridge.

words.trans: n. 藏身点，窝点
examples: The perfect hideout for someone up to no good.
The gang's hideout.

words.trans: adj. 像样的，正规的，标准的
examples: It's not even on a proper road.
a proper meal.

words.trans: 一条农场小路（a farm track of some sort 某条农场土路之类的）
examples: That dotted line must be a farm track.
We followed the farm track.

words.trans: n. 过路人，路人，途经此处的人（passers-by）
examples: No passers-by.
passers-by stopped to watch.

words.trans: 确凿地，有把握地（don’t know for certain that… 无法确凿断定）
examples: We don't know for certain that this is their base.
I can't say for certain.

words.trans: 固定短语：看样子，从表面来看。非常地道高频的英式口语表达，可日常使用；末尾的 it 不能随便换成别的名词（固定习语）
examples: It's going to be baking today, by the looks of it.
By the looks of it, we'll be late.

words.trans: n. 高山小湖，冰斗湖，湖区专用词汇
examples: Around that tarn.
The tarn lay below the ridge.

words.trans: n. 网格坐标，英国 OS 地图的方格定位编号（grid references）
examples: Maggie left the grid references for the tarn.
find the grid reference on a map.

words.trans: adj. 面容憔悴的，疲惫不堪的
examples: She looked haggard, Maggie thought.
He looked pale and haggard.

words.trans: n. 液体表面结出的薄皮、膜
examples: A skin of milk had formed on the top.
The soup had a skin.

words.trans: adj. 短暂的，时间不长的（briefly 短暂地，短短的，时间上一晃而过）
examples: I saw him briefly.
a brief visit.

words.trans: v. 使心神不宁；扰乱；使动摇
examples: She said something about unsettling him.
The news unsettled everyone.

words.trans: n.（监狱、精神病院、收容所等封闭机构里的）囚犯，被收容者，住院者
examples: Outside contact with inmates.
a young inmate.

words.trans: n. 折痕，褶皱；（脸上的）皱纹  v. 起折痕；弄皱；（面部）蹙起（crease up 英式口语：笑到弯腰、捧腹大笑，crease up with laughter 笑得直不起腰）
examples: She creased the newspaper along its fold.
crease up with laughter.

words.trans: 短语：镇定下来，平复情绪，收拾好心情（gather oneself together）
examples: Aunt Emily gathered herself together.
Take a moment to gather yourself together.

words.trans: n. 幽闭恐惧症
examples: Hasn't he told you about his claustrophobia?
He suffers from claustrophobia.

words.trans: n. 封闭狭小空间（enclosed spaces）
examples: He hates being in enclosed spaces.
the fear of enclosed spaces.

words.trans: n. 惊恐发作，心理上突发的强烈恐慌（panic attack）
examples: He had a panic attack in the tunnel.
She suffered panic attacks.

words.trans: n. 岩架，岩石突出的窄台
examples: Falling down past a ledge.
He hung from a ledge.

words.trans: 固定搭配：事情另有隐情，背后还有别的缘故，并不像表面看上去那么简单（I wonder if there was more to it. 我总觉得这事没那么简单/恐怕另有隐情）
examples: I wonder if there was more to it.
There's more to it than that.

words.trans: 用他所能发出最低沉的嗓音说话（in his deepest voice）
examples: He said in his deepest voice.
She said it in her deepest voice.

words.trans: 习语：睡得很香，睡得很沉（sleep like a baby）
examples: I slept like a baby.
He slept like a baby through the storm.

words.trans: 短语：实地探查；查看；结账（check out）
examples: It's time we checked out that farm.
We checked out the hotel online.

words.trans: 短语：猛地跳起来，一跃而起（spring up）
examples: Archie sprang up, sensing action.
He sprang up from his chair.

words.trans: n. 案件的线索，突破口（lead）
examples: It's the one lead we have to go on.
The police had no lead.

words.trans: 短语：作为依据（go on。something to go on 可以立足、赖以调查的线索凭据；nothing to go on 没有别的线索/凭据，没法往别的方向查）
examples: It's the one lead we have to go on.
They had nothing else to go on.

words.trans: 习语：图谋不轨，干坏事（up to no good）
examples: The perfect hideout for someone up to no good.
He's probably up to no good.

words.word: come at it a different way
words.trans: 短语：换个方向或方式靠近（come at it a different way）
examples: We need to come at it a different way.
Let's come at the problem a different way.

words.trans: 短语连词：既然那样，在这种情况下。承接上文事实，引出基于刚提到情况的推论、结果，常放句首后接逗号（It might rain, in which case we will cancel the walk.）
examples: It'll be baking; in which case, a second breakfast is in order.
It might rain, in which case we cancel.

words.trans: 习语：合乎情理，理应做某事（A celebration is in order. 是时候该庆祝一番了）
examples: A second breakfast might be in order.
A celebration is in order.

words.trans: 短语：考虑当下处境，在这种情况下（given the circumstances）
examples: Not surprising, given the circumstances.
Given the circumstances, we should wait.

words.trans: 短语：插嘴，打断别人说话（cut in）
examples: Joel cut in before she could speak.
Don't cut in while I'm talking.

words.trans: 短语连词：只要（so long as）
examples: So long as he's not cooped up in a small space.
You can go, so long as you're back by ten.

words.trans: 短语动词：将某人关在狭小空间，困住（coop up）
examples: Cooped up in a small space.
He hates being cooped up.

words.trans: have this thing about：对某件事抱有特殊的感受、心结、癖好、心理抵触，可喜欢可反感/心理阴影（看上下文）。固定口语习语，英式小说对话高频
examples: He has this thing about enclosed spaces.
I have this thing about the dark.

words.trans: 此处 properly 不是“恰当地、正确地”。英式口语典型用法：加强形容词/过去分词，表程度：真正地、实打实的（It’s the only thing he’s properly scared of. 这是他唯一真正害怕的事）
examples: It's the only thing he's properly scared of.
She was properly scared.

words.trans: 短语：说话突然中断（break off）
examples: She broke off, and wiped her eyes.
The talks broke off.

words.word: in a bit of a state
words.trans: 口语短语：状态糟糕，情绪慌乱（in a bit of a state）
examples: She was in a bit of a state.
She was in a bit of a state after the phone call.

words.trans: adj. 鲁莽的，冲动不计后果的。侧重考虑不周、仓促冲动，做事前没好好想清楚后果，多半一时脑子发热，不一定主观上想闯大祸。（与 reckless 区别：reckless 侧重明知有危险还是不在乎、肆意乱来，心里知道会有坏结果但根本不在意风险，语气比 rash 重，带“不顾安危”）
examples: It was a rash decision.
a rash assumption.
